title: Confidence Intervals for Off-Policy Evaluation at the Critical Overlap Boundary in Markov Decision Processes
banked_reason: terminal:laundering — oracle three-witness calibration replaced the frozen full-class minimax risk, honest finite-sample interval, and all-procedure lower-bound kernel.
gap_reasons: The core substitutes an oracle, three-witness Gaussian-calibration obstruction for the promised uniform minimax-MSE, globally honest finite-sample interval, and all-procedure lower-bound deliverable.

The note proves geometry-dependent Gaussian, Poisson, and mixed limits for three constructed triangular witness families and undercoverage of the note's own Gaussian-calibrated reset-cycle interval, not the advertised sharp minimax MSE, minimum honest expected length, or finite-sample honest inference over the full reset class.
proof_attempt_summary: D-1 accepted a pivot from the proposed full-class risk and interval frontier to critical local-limit witnesses. D0 derived three oracle-calibrated witness geometries and a Gaussian undercoverage example, with corrected and attested source comparisons. D0.5 found that the original uniform minimax MSE, computable globally honest finite-sample interval, and same-class all-procedure lower bound were not delivered; an independent validity check confirmed the kernel substitution. Reopening the original topic requires a new full-class upper proof, observable interval analysis, and lower experiment.
tldr: The three critical reset-cycle witnesses lie inside the factorized Mehrabi--Wager structural model as well as inside the maintained reset class.  Under their Theorem 4.1, the reset contraction \(q_T\) and action bound \(K_T\) induce \(\delta_T=-\log(q_T)/\log(K_T)\), so \(q_TK_T=1\) is exactly the published \(\delta=1\) MSE elbow.  Already at that elbow, diffuse rewards yield a Gaussian score, rare boundary rewards yield a centered-Poisson score, and mixtures yield a Gaussian--Poisson convolution; the Gaussian critical value therefore undercovers for this note's reset-cycle interval on a factorized boundary subclass.  This is a boundary-calibration obstruction for \(C_T(F_{\mathrm G})\), not a criticism of or claim about the Mehrabi--Wager TDR estimator, whose Gaussian theorem assumes a fixed exponent strictly larger than one.  Positive calibration remains limited to the three pre-specified witness geometries with oracle scale and law inputs.
gap: MehrabiWager2025 supplies Gaussian long-run inference only in its stated strictly supercritical weak-overlap regime and does not cover the equality boundary. KallusUehara2022 and HarariKermadec2011 give Gaussian or chi-square inference under regular bounded-ratio or fixed-score conditions. None of the inspected sources determines which critical value is justified for the growing reset-cycle score at \(qK=1\), and none is claimed to use the proposal-defined oracle interval.
fill: The local theorem derives Gaussian, centered-Poisson, and Gaussian--Poisson limits throughout the \(O(1/\log T)\) window and proves a model-internal nonuniform-calibration result: substituting \(c_{1-\alpha}(F_{\mathrm G})\) for \(c_{1-\alpha}(F)\) is not uniformly valid. The positive interval result is conditional on a pre-specified geometry and supplied oracle scale and calibration law; data-driven adaptation remains open.
